title: Chemical formulas
competency: Write formulas of elements and compounds and explain what a molecule is.

keywords.def: The symbolic representation of an element or a compound, like H₂O.
The smallest particle of an element or compound that has a stable, independent existence.
A molecule made of two atoms, like H₂ or O₂.
The small number after a symbol. In H₂O the 2 is a subscript.

en.text: A chemical formula is the symbolic representation of an element or a compound. Noble gases like helium exist as single atoms, so their formula is their symbol: He. Hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine exist as diatomic molecules: H₂, N₂, O₂, F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, I₂. Ozone is O₃, phosphorus P₄ and sulfur S₈.

screens.title: The oxygen we breathe
screens.ask: The oxygen we breathe: single O atoms, or two O atoms joined?
screens.after:
Oxygen gas is made of molecules of two atoms: O₂.
Oxygen is one of the diatomic elements in Table 3.3.

screens.title: 3.2.2 Chemical formulas
paras: A chemical formula is the symbolic representation of an element or a compound.
There are formulas of elements and formulas of compounds.
The formula of an element has one kind of symbol.

screens.title: Molecules
paras: A molecule is the smallest particle of an element or compound that has a stable, independent existence.
Helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon are noble gases.
They exist as single atoms (monoatomic). Their formula is the same as their symbol: He, Ne, Ar.

screens.title: Table 3.3: Diatomic elements
paras: Some non-metals exist as molecules of two atoms. They are diatomic molecules.
screens.note: Some molecules have more than two atoms: ozone O₃, phosphorus P₄, sulfur S₈.

root.label: Element molecules
root.info: The formula shows how many atoms are in one molecule.

children.label: Single atoms
children.info: Monoatomic. Noble gases. The formula is the same as the symbol.

children.label: He, Ne, Ar
children.info: Helium, neon and argon. Krypton, xenon and radon are single atoms too.

children.label: More than two
children.info: Some molecules have more than two atoms.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The symbolic representation of an element or a compound, like H₂O.
The smallest particle of an element or compound that has a stable, independent existence.
A molecule made of two atoms, like H₂ or O₂.

screens.text: Which formula shows a nitrogen molecule?
screens.why:
Nitrogen is a diatomic element (Table 3.3).
Its molecule has two N atoms.
Write the 2 as a subscript: N₂.
N alone is one atom; Ni is a different element.
Answer: N₂.

screens.title: How many atoms in the molecule?
screens.why:
Read the subscript: it counts the atoms.
He and Ne have no subscript: noble gases, single atoms.
Cl₂ and O₂ have the subscript 2: diatomic.
O₃ (ozone) has 3 and S₈ (sulfur) has 8: more than two atoms.
screens.clue: Count the atoms from the subscript.
screens.text: Sort each formula by the number of atoms in one molecule.
For which element are the atom formula and the molecule formula different?
screens.why:
Helium, argon and neon are noble gases.
They exist as single atoms, so atom and molecule formulas are the same.
Nitrogen is diatomic.
Its atom is N, but its molecule is N₂.
Answer: nitrogen.

screens.text: Tap every element whose molecule formula is the SAME as its symbol.
screens.why:
A formula equals the symbol only for single atoms.
Noble gases exist as single atoms: He, Ar, Ne.
H, Br and O are diatomic.
Their formulas are H₂, Br₂ and O₂, not the bare symbol.

en.text: A chemical formula with two or more different symbols stands for a compound. The small number after each symbol, the subscript, tells how many atoms of that element there are. In H₂O there are two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

screens.title: The small 2
screens.ask: In H₂O, what does the small 2 tell you?
screens.after:
The 2 is a subscript. It belongs to H, just before it.
So there are two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

screens.title: Formulas of compounds
paras: A formula of a compound has two or more different symbols.
Each symbol is followed by a subscript. It shows the number of atoms of that element.

screens.title: Reading H₂O
steps: H₂: the subscript 2 means 2 hydrogen atoms.
O: no subscript, so 1 oxygen atom.
So one water molecule has 2 H atoms and 1 O atom.

screens.title: Read the formula
screens.ask: Tap each formula to count its atoms.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The small number after a symbol. In H₂O the 2 is a subscript.

screens.ask: Read the formula CO₂: one carbon atom and ___ oxygen atoms.
screens.why:
C has no subscript: 1 carbon atom.
O has the subscript 2: 2 oxygen atoms.
Answer: 2.
screens.clue: Look at the number after O.

screens.text: Count the atoms of each element in CaCO₃ (calcium carbonate).
screens.why:
Ca has no subscript: 1 calcium atom.
C has no subscript: 1 carbon atom.
O has the subscript 3: 3 oxygen atoms.
Answer: Ca 1, C 1, O 3.
screens.clue: A symbol with no subscript has 1 atom.

screens.ask: Read the sugar formula C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁: there are ___ hydrogen atoms.
screens.why:
Each subscript belongs to the symbol just before it.
C₁₂: 12 carbon. H₂₂: 22 hydrogen. O₁₁: 11 oxygen.
Answer: 22 hydrogen atoms.
screens.clue: Find the number just after H.

screens.ask: Count all the atoms in one molecule of H₂SO₄: ___ atoms in total.
screens.why:
H₂: 2 hydrogen atoms.
S: 1 sulfur atom.
O₄: 4 oxygen atoms.
Total: 2 + 1 + 4 = 7.
Answer: 7.

items.text: Elements exist as diatomic and polyatomic molecules except which one?
items.why:
Phosphorus is polyatomic: P₄.
Nitrogen (N₂) and oxygen (O₂) are diatomic.
Neon is a noble gas.
It exists as single atoms: Ne.
Answer: neon.
items.clue: Which one is a noble gas?

items.text: For which element do the atom and the molecule have different formulas?
items.why:
Helium, argon and neon are noble gases.
They exist as single atoms, so atom and molecule formulas are the same.
Nitrogen is diatomic.
Its atom is N, but its molecule is N₂.
Answer: nitrogen.

test.text: What is the formula of hydrogen gas?
test.why:
Hydrogen is diatomic (Table 3.3).
Its molecule has two H atoms: H₂.
He is helium, a different element.
Answer: H₂.

test.text: True or false: the formula of helium is the same as its symbol, He.
test.why:
Helium is a noble gas.
Noble gases exist as single atoms.
So its formula is just its symbol: He.
The statement is true.

test.ask: Read the formula H₂O: there are ___ hydrogen atoms.
test.why:
The subscript 2 follows H.
So there are 2 hydrogen atoms.
O has no subscript: 1 oxygen atom.
Answer: 2.

Chlorine (Cl₂), iodine (I₂) and fluorine (F₂) are diatomic (Table 3.3).
Argon is a noble gas.
It exists as single atoms: Ar.
Answer: argon.

test.ask: Count all the atoms in one formula unit of NaHCO₃ (baking soda): ___ atoms.
test.why:
Na: 1 atom. H: 1 atom. C: 1 atom.
O₃: 3 atoms.
Total: 1 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 6.
Answer: 6.

notes.text: Krypton, xenon and radon are named in the book but have no symbol in Tables 3.1–3.2; not tested.
